body:
For anyone hitting this from a GDExtension, here's the workaround I shipped https://github.com/claytercek/godot-native-video/commit/a2e1e04cdedb5a0701ca1d4d6e47d586f496dec0

The idea is to donate the reference the driver is going to steal: after a successful `texture_create_from_extension`, do one extra `CFRetain` on the `MTLTexture`. Godot's unbalanced `release()` in `texture_free` then consumes the spare reference instead of your real one, and ownership comes out even.

Note: I avoided gating on an engine version. An unconditional retain leaks a texture per import on 4.6 and earlier (balanced driver), and a `>= 4.7` check inverts into the same leak the moment a fixed 4.7.x ships. Instead I'm probing the live driver once at init: hand `texture_create_from_extension` a throwaway 1x1 texture and compare `CFGetRetainCount` before and after the call. A balanced driver retains on import; the broken one leaves the count untouched. Donate only when the count didn't move, and the workaround stays correct on old versions, current 4.7, and whatever build eventually carries the fix.

I can confirm this on 4.8.dev 5902d3f37.

I bisected the regression to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/114484. cc @stuartcarnie 

> Godot v4.8.dev (5902d3f37) - macOS Tahoe (26.5.2) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M5 Max (Apple9) - Apple M5 Max (18 threads) - 48.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)
